title: Hackers exploit Tencent app flaw to deploy GrayRabbit malware
blurb: Problem: CVE-2026-51990, a one-click RCE flaw in Tencent's Sogou Input Method (huge China install base), exploited by China-aligned group UNC3569. Approach: A crafted sgbiz: link passes unvalidated args to Sogou's helper, opening an outdated, unsandboxed Chromium webview at an attacker URL, which exploits a known browser bug for code execution. Result: Installs a 64-bit GrayRabbit backdoor (reverse shells, file transfer, encrypted C2). Tencent patched the link handler in April; the browser stays outdated, unsandboxed. Why it matters: Trusted software with link handlers becomes an RCE chain once each step trusts the last unchecked — one patch doesn't fix the rest. Glossary: RCE (remote code execution) · URI handler (link protocol) · sandbox (code isolation) · C2 (attacker's control channel).

title: OpenAI Agents Linked to RubyGems Campaign That Gained RCE on RubyDoc Servers
blurb: AI agents were tied to a supply-chain campaign that turned malicious RubyGems packages into remote code execution on RubyDoc servers, another sign that agentic tooling is accelerating open-source supply-chain attacks.

title: Dutch NCSC: Critical Check Point VPN flaws exploitation is imminent
blurb: A national CSIRT is warning that active exploitation of critical Check Point VPN flaws is imminent, giving enterprises a narrow window to patch before mass scanning starts.

title: Moss developer Polyarc share that they're shutting down just two months after releasing a VR-less port of the beloved mousey adventure games
blurb: A well-regarded VR studio closing just months after diversifying beyond VR underscores how brutal the standalone VR market remains, even for critically loved games.

title: Warcraft 3: Reforged adds always-online requirement, removes LAN mode
blurb: Stripping LAN support and forcing an always-online connection on a 23-year-old RTS reignites debate over game preservation, ownership, and DRM in older titles still being patched.

title: Human embryo base editing can reach all cells but causes unpredictable genetic changes
blurb: Base editors can now reach every cell in a human embryo, but the unpredictable off-target genetic changes show germline editing still isn't controllable enough for clinical use.

title: Researchers pinpoint key early-universe measurement with record precision
blurb: A record-precision measurement tightens the constraints on early-universe physics, giving cosmologists a sharper benchmark to stress-test competing models against.

title: A 386 PC For Your RP2350
blurb: A cheap modern microcontroller emulating a full 386 PC shows how far hobbyist emulation on commodity hardware has come since the era it's recreating.

title: I made a build visualizer to understand Bun's compile times
blurb: A homemade profiler that visualizes Bun's build pipeline shows how much insight into compile-time bottlenecks is hidden in tools most developers never open.

title: Analyzing the FScale Instruction in Intel's 8087 FPU
blurb: Problem: How does the 8087, the coprocessor whose design shaped IEEE 754 float math, implement something as "simple" as FSCALE — scaling by a power of two? Approach: Ken Shirriff reverse-engineered the 8087's microcode and die layout, tracing which circuit blocks fire when FSCALE runs. Result: The "trivial" math takes 140+ micro-instructions across three subroutine levels, handling register loads, edge cases, errors, and stack management before returning an answer. Why it matters: It reveals the hardware cost behind "basic" float math, and how the 8087's rigor became the template for IEEE 754, used by nearly every computer. Glossary: microcode (hardware instructions for a CPU instruction) · FPU (floating-point unit) · IEEE 754 (float standard) · die shot (chip layout photo).
